name: Employee Card

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a Czech employer (not classified as an 'unreliable employer' under Czech law) and a job vacancy registered in the Central Database of Job Vacancies, unless the applicant already has free labour-market access.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a qualifying job offer with a registered vacancy.

evidence_required.document: Confirmation of registered job vacancy (Central Database of Job Vacancies)

outcome.duration_length: up to 2 years, may be restricted to the duration of employment or work-permit validity

sources.title: ipc.gov.cz -- Employee Card: employer/vacancy requirements, 2-year duration cap, 90-day grace period on job loss

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Czechia's initial build. Confirmed directly at tier-1. A separate 'non-dual' Employee Card variant exists for nationals of nine countries with free labour-market access (as of 1 July 2024) who can change employers freely with 3-day notification, and does not require a registered-vacancy match -- not modelled as a fully separate route here given limited detail on which nine countries qualify, but flagged as a materially easier variant of this same permit category. Minimum salary was not specified at tier-1 in this pass. family_can_join set false: not addressed in the source for this specific permit (family members would apply separately via cz_family_reunification, which requires the employee-card-holder sponsor to have resided in Czechia 6+ months). If employment ends without alternative labour-market access, holders have 90 days to secure new employment or another residence basis before losing status.
